When the diagnostic imaging rule is applied, diagnostic imaging procedures are grouped based on their Diagnostic Imaging Family Indicator (typically based on the value from the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule). This procedure's family indicator is 88. Then within each group, procedures are paid by splitting them into their Professional Component (PC) and Technical Component (TC). To rank the procedures, it splits the technical and professional components and calculates the allowed amounts for each procedure. To evaluate the technical component, the allowed amount is calculated as if the charge had a TC modifier. For the Professional Component it does the same with a 26 modifier. It then ranks the procedures by the sum of the resulting technical and professional components. The highest priced procedure is reimbursed at 100%, for both components. Subsequent procedures within the family have a defined PC percentage applied to their PC part, and a defined TC percentage applied to their TC part.  The first of the following criteria that the procedure qualifies for will determine if the diagnostic imaging rule is applied, the PC%, and the TC%:  Meets criteria defined by "SHC PB NON PCTC SPLIT PROCS": Applies; PC% of 95%; TC% of 50%;  Default: Does not apply        If the allowed amount exceeds the billed amount, it will be capped at the billed amount.

When the diagnostic imaging rule is applied, diagnostic imaging procedures are grouped based on their Diagnostic Imaging Family Indicator (typically based on the value from the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule). This procedure's family indicator is 88. Then within each group, procedures are paid by splitting them into their Professional Component (PC) and Technical Component (TC). To rank the procedures, it splits the technical and professional components and calculates the allowed amounts for each procedure. To evaluate the technical component, the allowed amount is calculated as if the charge had a TC modifier. For the Professional Component it does the same with a 26 modifier. It then ranks the procedures by the sum of the resulting technical and professional components. The highest priced procedure is reimbursed at 100%, for both components. Subsequent procedures within the family have a defined PC percentage applied to their PC part, and a defined TC percentage applied to their TC part.  The first of the following criteria that the procedure qualifies for will determine if the diagnostic imaging rule is applied, the PC%, and the TC%:  Meets criteria defined by "SHC PB NON PCTC SPLIT PROCS": Applies; PC% of 95%; TC% of 50%;  Default: Does not apply        If the allowed amount exceeds the billed amount, it will be capped at the billed amount.

payers_information.standard_charge_algorithm: Fee schedule rate ($341.14).    This procedure could have the ophthalmology rule applied to it.  When a claim contains two or more procedures that the ophthalmology rule applies to with the same date of service, they are considered together for the ophthalmology reduction.  If the procedures are reported as global diagnostic procedures (i.e. without 26 or TC modifier) and with the same date of service, each procedure is split (for calculation purposes only) into the professional component (PC) and is given the 26 modifier and technical component (TC) and is given the TC modifier. If the procedures are reported with a TC modifier, the internal split does not happen. The procedures are then ranked by the calculated allowed amount of the TC component. The procedure with the highest rank will be reimbursed at 100% of its allowed amount and subsequent procedures will have the TC calculated at a defined TC percentage. If a split was performed, the professional component is added back to get the allowed amount for the procedure.  The first of the following criteria that the procedure qualifies for will determine if the ophthalmology rule is applied and the TC%:  Meets criteria defined by "SHC PB NON PCTC SPLIT PROCS": Applies; TC% of 80%;  Default: Does not apply        If the allowed amount exceeds the billed amount, it will be capped at the billed amount.

If a split was performed, the professional component is added back to get the allowed amount for the procedure.
